subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Transparency in Nudging
description: A 60-second lesson on Transparency in Nudging.

hook.text: Should governments disclose that they use nudges? A survey found 86% of people support nudges, but only when told about.

buildup.text: Transparency means telling citizens that behavioral techniques are being used.

discovery.text: Loewenstein found that disclosed nudges are nearly as effective as secret ones. Transparency doesn't destroy the effect.

twist.text: Some nudges lose power when disclosed. If you know a countdown timer is fake, it stops working.

climax.text: Transparency is a test: if a nudge still works when people know about it, it's legitimate.

punchline.text: If the nudge survives disclosure, it deserves to stay.

quiz.question: Why is the 'transparency test' useful for evaluating nudges?
options: All nudges fail when disclosed, so the test identifies them
If a nudge works after disclosure, it is legitimate; if it fails, it was manipulation
